In the question below, some statements are followed by two conclusions I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, decide which conclusion(s) definitely follow.

Statements: U ≤ T ≤ W ≤ V = S

Conclusions:
I. U < V
II. U = V

steps: Combine the statements: U ≤ T ≤ W ≤ V = S.
Conclusion I (U < V): derived relation is U ≤ V → does not follow definitely.
Conclusion II (U = V): derived relation is U ≤ V → does not follow definitely.
Conclusions I and II involve the same pair, are mutually exclusive and together cover every possibility → either I or II follows.
Checked by enumerating every ordering of the letters consistent with the statements.
explanation.formula_used: A relation follows only if it holds in every ordering consistent with the statements; opposite signs (> then <) break the chain
explanation.trap: Do not read across opposite-direction signs; ≥ combined with > gives >, but ≥ with ≥ gives only ≥.

questions.subject: general-intelligence-reasoning
questions.stem: In which of the following expressions is the expression 'F < D' definitely true?

steps: Trace F and D along each expression; the path between them must have every sign pointing the same way.
In 'F < D = E < C = B', the path from F to D makes 'F < D' definitely true.
In each other expression the path contains an opposite sign or a weak sign, so the relation is either uncertain or the opposite of what is required.
Verified by enumerating every ordering consistent with each expression.
explanation.formula_used: Relation between two letters is definite only if every sign on the path between them points the same way
explanation.trap: A single opposite sign anywhere between the two letters destroys the relation; ≥ with > still gives >.

questions.stem:
In the question below, some statements are followed by two conclusions I and II. Take the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, and decide which of the conclusions logically follow.

Statements:
All bottles are chairs.
Some teachers are chairs.

Conclusions:
I. Some bottles are chairs.
II. No teacher is a chair.

steps: Draw the least-overlap (Venn) case for the statements: All bottles are chairs. Some teachers are chairs.
Conclusion I: Some bottles are chairs. → true in every valid diagram → follows.
Conclusion II: No teacher is a chair. → false in every valid diagram → does not follow.
Verified by enumerating all 20 admissible Venn-region models in the builder.
explanation.formula_used: Definite conclusion: true in every valid Venn diagram; possibility: true in at least one; either-or: complementary pair, neither definite
explanation.trap: Test the definite conclusions on the least-overlap diagram; a possibility follows unless a statement rules it out.
